symbols.name: A
symbols.def: Randomized assignment, with control coded by \(0\) and treatment coded by \(1\).

symbols.name: Y0
symbols.def: \(Y_0=Y(0)\) is the favorable latent outcome under control.

symbols.name: Y1
symbols.def: \(Y_1=Y(1)\) is the favorable latent outcome under treatment.

symbols.name: W0
symbols.def: \(W_0=W(0)\) is the assay-recorded outcome under control.

symbols.name: W1
symbols.def: \(W_1=W(1)\) is the assay-recorded outcome under treatment.

symbols.name: W
symbols.def: The observed recorded endpoint selected by assignment.

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: The joint law of \(A,Y_0,Y_1,W_0,W_1,W\).

symbols.name: q0
symbols.def: \(q_0=P(W=1\mid A=0)\), defined under \(P(A=0)>0\).

symbols.name: q1
symbols.def: \(q_1=P(W=1\mid A=1)\), defined under \(P(A=1)>0\).

symbols.name: s
symbols.def: The common probability that the assay records a favorable outcome when the latent outcome is favorable.

symbols.name: c
symbols.def: The common probability that the assay records an unfavorable outcome when the latent outcome is unfavorable.

symbols.name: kappa
symbols.def: A fixed lower bound on the Youden index.

symbols.name: uL
symbols.def: \(u_L\) is the lower endpoint of the false-positive rectangle coordinate.

symbols.name: uU
symbols.def: \(u_U\) is the upper endpoint of the false-positive rectangle coordinate.

symbols.name: vL
symbols.def: \(v_L\) is the lower endpoint of the true-positive rectangle coordinate.

symbols.name: vU
symbols.def: \(v_U\) is the upper endpoint of the true-positive rectangle coordinate.

symbols.name: thetaL
symbols.def: \(\theta_L\) is the fixed lower endpoint of the latent association band.

symbols.name: thetaU
symbols.def: \(\theta_U\) is the fixed upper endpoint of the latent association band.

symbols.name: theta
symbols.def: \(\theta\) indexes a member of the finite association band.

symbols.name: r
symbols.def: \(r=\theta-1\).

symbols.name: Bcoef
symbols.def: \(B=1-r\Delta\).

symbols.name: D
symbols.def: \(D=\{(u,v):u_L\le u\le\min(u_U,q_0,q_1),\ \max(v_L,q_0,q_1)\le v\le v_U,\ v-u\ge\kappa\}\).

symbols.name: btheta
symbols.def: The probability-compatible root after substituting the shared-channel corrected margins.

symbols.name: Ctheta
symbols.def: The feasible vertices and boundary contacts specified in \(\mathrm{def:candidate-map}\).

symbols.name: L
symbols.def: \(L=\min_{z\in C_{\theta_U}}b_{\theta_U}(z)\).

symbols.name: U
symbols.def: \(U=\max_{z\in C_{\theta_L}}b_{\theta_L}(z)\).

symbols.name: n0
symbols.def: \(n_0\) is the fixed control-arm sample size.

symbols.name: n1
symbols.def: \(n_1\) is the fixed treatment-arm sample size.

symbols.name: m1
symbols.def: \(m_1\) is the gold-standard true-positive stratum size.

symbols.name: m0
symbols.def: \(m_0\) is the gold-standard true-negative stratum size.

symbols.name: T0
symbols.def: \(T_0\) counts recorded favorable outcomes in the control arm.

symbols.name: T1
symbols.def: \(T_1\) counts recorded favorable outcomes in the treatment arm.

symbols.name: V1
symbols.def: \(V_1\) counts assay positives among gold-standard positives.

symbols.name: V0
symbols.def: \(V_0\) counts assay negatives among gold-standard negatives.

symbols.name: beta
symbols.def: \(\beta\) is the target simultaneous noncoverage probability.

symbols.name: beta0
symbols.def: \(\beta_0\) is the control-risk noncoverage budget.

symbols.name: beta1
symbols.def: \(\beta_1\) is the treatment-risk noncoverage budget.

symbols.name: betaS
symbols.def: \(\beta_s\) is the sensitivity noncoverage budget.

symbols.name: betaC
symbols.def: \(\beta_c\) is the specificity noncoverage budget.

symbols.name: Q0
symbols.def: \(Q_0\) is the two-sided Clopper--Pearson interval from \(T_0\) with noncoverage \(\beta_0\).

symbols.name: Q1
symbols.def: \(Q_1\) is the two-sided Clopper--Pearson interval from \(T_1\) with noncoverage \(\beta_1\).

symbols.name: Sint
symbols.def: \(S\) is the two-sided Clopper--Pearson interval from \(V_1\) with noncoverage \(\beta_s\).

symbols.name: Cint
symbols.def: \(C\) is the two-sided Clopper--Pearson interval from \(V_0\) with noncoverage \(\beta_c\).

symbols.name: Fhat
symbols.def: The compatible trial-risk and channel tuples retained by the four primitive intervals, the fixed channel rectangle, and the informativeness floor.

symbols.name: Ibeta
symbols.def: \(I_{\beta}\) is the interval image of \(\widehat{\mathcal F}\times[\theta_L,\theta_U]\) through the compatible-root map.

symbols.name: Kstar
symbols.def: \(K^{\star}=[b_{\theta_U}(u,v),b_{\theta_L}(u,v)]\) at the population trial risks and transported true channel.

symbols.name: Mstar
symbols.def: \(M^{\star}\) is the smallest number of channel evaluations sufficient in the worst case to recover one endpoint over the stated polygon family.

assumptions.condition: The sensitivity and specificity in the blinded gold-standard validation population equal the trial-channel quantities \(s\) and \(c\).

definitions.name: closed shared-assay odds-band model
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cl}}=\{P:(A,Y_0,Y_1,W_0,W_1,W)\text{ satisfies randomization, assignment positivity, consistency, the two common-channel equalities, the channel rectangle, }d\ge\kappa,\text{ and the closed cross-product band}\}\).

definitions.name: probability-compatible benefit root
definitions.construction: For \(p_0=(q_0-u)/(v-u)\), \(p_1=(q_1-u)/(v-u)\), \(\Delta=p_1-p_0\), \(r=\theta-1\), \(B=1-r\Delta\), and \(C=p_1(1-p_0)\), define \[b_{\theta}(u,v)=\begin{cases}C,&\theta=1,\\(-B+\sqrt{B^2+4rC})/(2r),&\theta\ne1.\end{cases}\] The second branch is evaluated by its algebraically equivalent stable form when cancellation would occur.

definitions.name: ten-point channel candidate map
definitions.construction: \(C_{\theta}\) is obtained by retaining feasible points from: every vertex of \(D\); every intersection of an axis-aligned edge of \(D\) with \(u+v=q_0+q_1+\sqrt{\theta}|q_1-q_0|\) or \(u+v=q_0+q_1-\sqrt{\theta}|q_1-q_0|\); and, on the edge \(v-u=\kappa\), the point satisfying \(u+v=q_0+q_1\). Duplicate points are removed.

definitions.name: attaining four-type law and assay coupling
definitions.construction: Given a feasible \((u,v,\theta)\), assign masses \((p_{00},p_{01},p_{10},p_{11})=(1-p_0-b,b,b-\Delta,p_1-b)\) at \(b=b_{\theta}(u,v)\). Conditional on \(Y_a\), generate \(W_a\) with \(P(W_a=1\mid Y_a)=u+(v-u)Y_a\), and randomize \(A\) independently.

definitions.name: exact primitive-set projection
definitions.construction: Let \(Q_a\), \(S\), and \(C\) be the four Clopper--Pearson intervals. Define \[\widehat{\mathcal F}=\{(\widetilde q_0,\widetilde q_1,\widetilde u,\widetilde v):\widetilde q_a\in Q_a,\ \widetilde v\in S\cap[v_L,v_U],\ 1-\widetilde u\in C,\ \widetilde u\in[u_L,u_U],\ \widetilde u\le\widetilde q_a\le\widetilde v,\ \widetilde v-\widetilde u\ge\kappa\}.\] Define \(I_{\beta}\) as the interval image of \(\widehat{\mathcal F}\times[\theta_L,\theta_U]\) through the compatible-root construction.

definitions.name: oriented boundary-arrangement handle
definitions.construction: Classify realizable incidences among the at most five polygon vertices, the two slope \(-1\) stationary lines, and the slope \(1\) informativeness edge; use oriented sign patterns and endpoint-preserving perturbations to derive a universal evaluation cap and a matching configuration.

statements.statement: For every law satisfying the shared sensitivity and specificity equalities with \(d\ge\kappa\), the latent margins obey \(p_a=(q_a-u)/(v-u)\). A channel is probability-compatible if and only if it belongs to \(D\).
statements.justification: The common channel couples the two corrected margins, so its exact feasible polygon is the first nonseparable object.
statements.gap: Molinari2008 gives a general linear channel system; this lemma specializes it to one common binary assay and records the exact joint compatibility polygon.
statements.consumer: The polygon is the feasible domain used by every endpoint and confidence-projection calculation.

statements.statement: Fix \(z=(u,v)\in D\) and \(\theta\in[\theta_L,\theta_U]\). On \([\max(0,\Delta),\min(p_1,1-p_0)]\), the equation \[(\theta-1)b^2+\{1-(\theta-1)\Delta\}b-p_1(1-p_0)=0\] has exactly one root, namely \(b_{\theta}(z)\) from \(\mathrm{def:compatible-root}\), and its four masses from \(\mathrm{def:attaining-law}\) are nonnegative and satisfy \(p_{11}p_{00}=\theta p_{10}p_{01}\).
statements.justification: A unique probability-compatible branch prevents algebraic root selection from contaminating sharpness.
statements.gap: ZhangNieSoonLiu2013, Section 3.3, reconstructs a positive \(2\times2\) table at fixed clean margins; this lemma includes structural-zero margins created at assay-feasibility contacts.
statements.consumer: The selected branch is the evaluable objective for certified endpoint enumeration.

statements.statement: The compatible-root map is continuous on \(D\times[\theta_L,\theta_U]\), nonincreasing in \(\theta\), nonincreasing in \(p_0\), and nondecreasing in \(p_1\). Wherever differentiated, \[\frac{\partial b}{\partial\theta}=-\frac{p_{01}p_{10}}{\theta(p_{01}+p_{10})+p_{11}+p_{00}},\quad -1\le\frac{\partial b}{\partial p_0}\le0,\quad 0\le\frac{\partial b}{\partial p_1}\le1.\] These inequalities extend to boundary contacts by continuity.
statements.justification: Monotonicity profiles out the odds band and supplies the uniform Lipschitz control used in inference.
statements.gap: CiocaneaTeodorescuGabrielSjolander2025 studies a clean-outcome marginal sensitivity parameter; it does not derive comparative statics through a shared uncertain assay polygon.
statements.consumer: The derivative bounds reduce optimization to \(\theta_U\) for the lower endpoint and \(\theta_L\) for the upper endpoint.

statements.statement: If \(D\neq\varnothing\), the identified set of \(b=P(Y_0=0,Y_1=1)\) over \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cl}}\) is exactly \([L,U]\). Each endpoint is attained by the construction in \(\mathrm{def:attaining-law}\). For each fixed odds endpoint, \(C_{\theta}\) is complete and contains at most ten distinct channels: at most five vertices, at most four axis-edge contacts with the two stationary lines, and at most one stationary point on \(v-u=\kappa\). Without the informativeness cut, at most eight channels suffice.
statements.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: a nonlinear sharp set becomes a constant-size, closed-form candidate map with constructive attainment.
statements.gap: ZhangNieSoonLiu2013 fixes clean margins and Molinari2008 leaves general channel restrictions to nonlinear programming; neither supplies the shared-channel stationary-line completeness theorem.
statements.consumer: A validation-enabled trial analyst can compute sharp benefit bounds without trusting a generic nonlinear optimizer at feasibility edges.

statements.statement: If \(D^{\circ}\neq\varnothing\), the infimum and supremum of \(b\) over \(\mathcal M_{+}\) equal \(L\) and \(U\). The lower endpoint is attained in \(\mathcal M_{+}\) if and only if some \(z\in C_{\theta_U}\cap D^{\circ}\) satisfies \(b_{\theta_U}(z)=L\); the upper endpoint is attained if and only if some \(z\in C_{\theta_L}\cap D^{\circ}\) satisfies \(b_{\theta_L}(z)=U\).
statements.justification: Strict log-odds models can lose endpoint attainment at marginal contacts even when their closure has the same bounds.
statements.gap: CiocaneaTeodorescuGabrielSjolander2025 assumes positive cells; the exact closure-to-strict transfer and finite attainment criterion under assay uncertainty are not given there.
statements.consumer: Software and applied reports can distinguish an attained sharp bound from a merely approachable sensitivity limit.

statements.statement: When \(s=c=1\), the compatible-root formula reduces to the fixed-clean-margin binary odds reconstruction of ZhangNieSoonLiu2013. When additionally \(\theta_L=\theta_U=1\), it reduces to \(b=p_1(1-p_0)\). For the synthetic box \(q_0=1/5\), \(q_1=3/10\), \(u\in[1/20,1/10]\), \(v\in[4/5,9/10]\), \(\theta\in[1,4]\), and \(\kappa\le7/10\), the endpoints are \((\sqrt{193}-5)/48\) and \(4/15\), both attained by positive-cell laws.
statements.justification: Known-case collapse and an exact nondegenerate witness guard the candidate algebra against sign and root-selection errors.
statements.gap: The clean-assay reductions are prior art; the exact uncertain-assay witness is a diagnostic specialization of the new envelope rather than an independent novelty claim.
statements.consumer: The exact values provide regression tests for a certified implementation and a transparent worked example for trial analysts.

statements.statement: Under assignment positivity, the four marginal binomial sampling laws, validation transport, and the confidence-budget condition, \[\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cl}}}\Pr_P\{K^{\star}\subseteq I_{\beta}\}\ge1-\beta.\] No mutual-independence condition on \(T_0,T_1,V_1,V_0\) is required. Coverage holds uniformly through optimizer ties, marginal contacts, and collapsed faces. Moreover, each endpoint of \(I_{\beta}\) is computable by a four-region profiling rule: the nontrivial root region uses the ten-point map, the two fractional regions use polygon vertices, and the constant region uses a feasibility check. Applied to \(\mathrm{def:kill-test-witness}\), the lower projection retains the legal edge value \(0.1320580555\) to the displayed precision.
statements.justification: Exact primitive inversion avoids branchwise bootstrap failures and remains valid at every nonsmooth contact.
statements.gap: GabrielSachsJensen2024 evaluates bootstrap coverage, documents regular-bootstrap undercoverage near boundaries, and reports a conservative \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) correction; FanPark2010 and KaidoMolinariStoye2019 provide adjacent clean-bound and generic projection inference. None gives exact simultaneous validation-binomial projection through the finite contact-complete shared-assay evaluator.
statements.consumer: A prospective BNT162b2-style endpoint study with a blinded validation substudy obtains a uniformly valid confidence set for its full true-channel benefit interval.

statements.statement: Under assignment positivity, let \(N_j=(n_0,n_1,m_1,m_0)\), \(w_j=(1,1,2,2)\), and \(\varepsilon_j=\sqrt{\log(2/\beta_j)/(2N_j)}\). Uniformly over compatible primitives with \(d\ge\kappa\), with probability at least \(1-\beta\), \[K^{\star}\subseteq I_{\beta}\subseteq[\inf K^{\star}-R,\sup K^{\star}+R]\cap[0,1],\qquad R=\frac{2}{\kappa}\sum_jw_j\varepsilon_j.\] In addition, \(\sup_P E_P[\{\operatorname{length}(I_{\beta})-\operatorname{length}(K^{\star})\}_{+}]=O(1/(\kappa\sqrt{N_{\min}}))\) for fixed marginal budgets. These claims use only the four marginal binomial laws and do not require their counts to be mutually independent.
statements.justification: Coverage alone can be vacuous; the width theorem quantifies the statistical price of weak assay informativeness and four primitive intervals.
statements.gap: KaidoMolinariStoye2019 establishes uniform asymptotic coverage for generic moment projections but not an exact finite-sample width modulus indexed by the Youden floor.
statements.consumer: Validation-study designers can translate a desired benefit-interval precision into trial and gold-standard stratum sizes.

statements.statement: Determine \(M^{\star}\), the smallest universal worst-case number of distinct channel evaluations required to recover one sharp endpoint over all nonempty feasible polygons in this model. Establish both a reduction from the ten-point map and a realizable configuration proving that no smaller cap suffices, while preserving endpoint attainment in the strict model.
statements.justification: The proved constant-size map need not be combinatorially minimal, and minimality is the honest open mathematical content beyond completeness.
statements.gap: No cited benefit-bound or misclassification paper studies the worst-case evaluation complexity of a shared-channel semialgebraic envelope.
statements.consumer: A sharp cap yields the smallest auditable branch set for exact arithmetic and formal verification.

sampling_model.design: A blinded two-arm randomized trial with a separate blinded gold-standard validation sample.
sampling_model.units: Trial and validation samples have fixed positive sizes \(n_0,n_1,m_1,m_0\); the four stated marginal count laws are sufficient, with no mutual-independence requirement among the counts.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary randomized assignment \(A\) with positive allocation probability in each arm.
sampling_model.overlap: The assay satisfies the uniform informativeness restriction \(s+c-1\ge\kappa>0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Two-sided Clopper--Pearson intervals are formed separately for \(q_0,q_1,s,c\) and intersected with the fixed assay rectangle before projection.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: A binary joint table can be recovered from its two margins and a fixed positive odds ratio.
Direct misclassification writes the observed and latent discrete distributions as a linear system with a restricted channel matrix.

For symbolic ordinal benefit bounds, the regular bootstrap can undercover near parameter-space boundaries, while an \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) bootstrap correction is conservative in the reported simulations.
Calibrated projection gives uniformly asymptotically valid confidence intervals for smooth functions in finite moment-restriction models.
A single marginal sensitivity parameter identifies probability of benefit without growing with covariate dimension.
Warning accuracy for a misclassified randomization test can be computed through adaptive integer programming.

tldr: Average efficacy can conceal simultaneous benefit and harm, while an imperfect binary endpoint assay makes even the two latent arm risks uncertain and couples them through one blinded channel. The proposal derives a unique probability-compatible latent-table root and proves that the sharp probability-of-benefit interval under a finite cross-product odds band is obtained from at most ten explicit channel candidates. It constructs attaining laws, separates closed-model endpoints from strict positive-cell attainment, and projects four exact binomial confidence sets through a finite contact-robust map with excess width of order \(1/(\kappa\sqrt{N_{\min}})\).

project_justification.gap: Binary probability-of-benefit sensitivity analyses take the latent arm margins as observed, while direct misclassification methods do not exploit the special coupling created by one uncertain assay channel or the finite odds-band root geometry. Existing bound-inference work does not give finite-sample validation-binomial coverage through ties and assay-feasibility contacts.
project_justification.niche: A shared channel converts two separate margin intervals into a two-dimensional convex polygon whose nonlinear odds-root objective has an unusually small and explicitly classifiable stationary set.
project_justification.fill: The paper supplies the complete ten-candidate envelope, constructive sharpness, an exact strict-attainment criterion, and exact primitive confidence projection with a Youden-index width modulus.

related_work: ZhangNieSoonLiu2013, Section 3.3, supplies the fixed-margin binary odds reconstruction adapted in the compatible-root lemma. CiocaneaTeodorescuGabrielSjolander2025, Theorem 1 and its discussion of compatibility, provides the closest clean-outcome probability-of-benefit sensitivity formulation and the motivation arc from cancellation of benefit and harm. Molinari2008, equations (2.1)--(2.3), supplies the direct channel-matrix view and constructive interpretation of sharp latent distributions. GabrielSachsJensen2024 derives symbolic ordinal benefit bounds, evaluates bootstrap coverage, documents regular-bootstrap undercoverage near parameter-space boundaries, and reports a conservative \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) correction. The inference novelty here is limited to exact simultaneous inversion of the trial-risk and validation binomials coupled with the finite contact-complete shared-assay evaluator. FanPark2010 develops inference for switching sharp treatment-effect-distribution bounds. KaidoMolinariStoye2019 supplies the calibrated-projection comparison, although the present procedure uses exact binomial inversion rather than asymptotic calibration. RossColeEdwardsEtAl2024 makes assay transport an explicit data-fusion condition rather than an implication of blinding. HengShaw2025 treats finite-population randomization tests under misclassification and motivates certified edge handling, but its target is warning accuracy rather than a superpopulation benefit interval. PolackEtAl2020 supplies the prospective clinical workflow: a blinded vaccine trial with a laboratory-confirmed binary endpoint, not evidence that a transported common assay channel already holds.
technical_internal_limitation: A floating-point generic optimizer missed a legal informativeness-edge minimum, returning \(0.1443566356\) instead of the explicit candidate value \(0.1320580555\). This is an implementation diagnostic, not a theorem contribution. Exact feasibility predicates and outward-rounded root evaluation remain necessary before empirical deployment.
honest_scope: The closed-model envelope, strict-attainment transfer, exact projection, and width rate are all posed as results to prove. The minimal universal evaluation cap is deliberately left as an open-ended question. Assay transport is maintained prospectively and is not inferred from trial blinding. Infinite odds endpoints, zero informativeness, covariate-dependent channels, and an empirical reanalysis of PolackEtAl2020 are outside the formal claim.

seed_details.anchor: ZhangNieSoonLiu2013, Section 3.3, together with CiocaneaTeodorescuGabrielSjolander2025, Theorem 1 and Discussion
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The fixed clean margins in the binary odds-root reconstruction are replaced by the joint affine inversion \(p_a=(q_a-u)/(v-u)\) through one common uncertain channel; endpoint analysis therefore starts with a coupled polygon rather than two independent intervals.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining probability of benefit, shared sensitivity and specificity, outcome misclassification, odds-ratio bands, stationary lines, and sharp bounds found no primary theorem with this target--method pair.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: this is immediate from ZhangNieSoonLiu2013 followed by optimizing two corrected risks. Rebuttal: a common channel prevents separate margin optimization, and the complete edge-contact classification includes legal nonvertex extrema and structural-zero contacts absent from that paper.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed uses an explicit non-LP algebraic envelope and a finite candidate theorem, not an unspecified optimization problem.

seed_details.anchor: GabrielSachsJensen2024, bootstrap coverage study, and KaidoMolinariStoye2019, Theorem 3.1
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Regular and \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) bootstrap approximations and calibrated asymptotics are replaced by simultaneous exact inversion of four marginal binomials, after which coverage follows from Bonferroni set containment and endpoint computation requires profiling a moving polytope across contact regions.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for exact binomial projection of probability-of-benefit bounds with validation sensitivity and specificity found no contact-uniform finite evaluator or explicit Youden-index width bound.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: Bonferroni projection is generic and therefore not publishable. Rebuttal: generic coverage is credited; the new content is the finite four-region reduction tied to the ten-candidate causal envelope and its uniform width modulus.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Inference is an attached rung to an explicit identified-set representation, not a bare M8 label.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Point substitution of transported sensitivity and specificity becomes optimization over a bounded discrepancy set between validation and trial channels; the first new object is the smallest discrepancy radius at which zero enters the benefit interval.
seed_details.destination_search: The transport paper identifies risks and risk differences under point transport, while searches coupling bounded assay transport with cross-world benefit odds bands found no critical-radius theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: adding a transport box only enlarges the existing channel rectangle. Rebuttal: a scientifically indexed discrepancy path and its critical sign radius would require a parametric envelope and frontier theorem, not a relabelled box.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The critical discrepancy radius is a named scalar target; simple qualitative widening would not count.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace general nonlinear-program estimation of a channel region by an oriented incidence classification that seeks the smallest worst-case endpoint evaluation set.
seed_details.destination_search: No searched misclassification or benefit-bound source gives a lower bound on finite endpoint-enumeration complexity.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: shaving ten candidates is implementation trivia. Rebuttal: it becomes mathematical only with a universal reduction and matching realizable lower-bound configuration; absent both it is retained solely as the proposal's open question.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: A single hand-tuned witness is insufficient; the lower bound must describe a nondegenerate realizable configuration.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The common affine inverse is replaced by two arm-specific channel inverses linked by a departure constraint, increasing the nuisance dimension from two to four and destroying the planar stationary-line proof.
seed_details.destination_search: HengShaw2025 optimizes finite-population error patterns for tests; searches found no superpopulation probability-of-benefit envelope with differential channels and a latent odds band.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: this is merely the shared-channel result with two extra coordinates. Rebuttal: the constant-size enumeration may fail in four dimensions, so a credible paper needs either a new semialgebraic certificate or a nonrepresentability theorem.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed would be rejected if phrased as routine dimensional extension; the missing constant-size certificate is substantive.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Treat the positive and negative validation-stratum sizes as design variables and minimize worst-case projected benefit width subject to a fixed validation budget, certifying the allocation by a matching lower bound or Karush--Kuhn--Tucker conditions.
seed_details.destination_search: The transport paper discusses the cost and richness of validation data but does not optimize stratum allocation for a partially identified cross-world target.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: Neyman allocation immediately solves the problem. Rebuttal: the active endpoint branch and \(1/\kappa\) propagation weights switch with the unknown channel, so the minimax design is not the ordinary variance allocation.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: A candidate allocation without an optimality certificate would not satisfy M13.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The fixed ordinal margins in the transportation-polytope argument become inverse images under one uncertain multicategory confusion matrix, and local cross-product restrictions add nonlinear coupling among table cells.
seed_details.destination_search: LuDingDasgupta2018 and GabrielSachsJensen2024 treat clean ordinal margins; Molinari2008 treats multicategory channels but not cross-world benefit couplings.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: compose Molinari's matrix restrictions with Lu's linear program. Rebuttal: with an unknown shared confusion matrix and total-positivity restrictions the feasible image is bilinear, so sharpness and a practical representation do not follow by LP composition.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The natural substrate is a non-LP coupling problem, so an automatic LP label would be misleading.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace conditional stratumwise odds reconstruction by a single marginal odds-band equation after integrating conditional four-type laws, while one assay channel simultaneously corrects every stratum.
seed_details.destination_search: The anchor uses one marginal sensitivity parameter with clean outcomes; searches found no theorem combining that global association coordinate with a shared uncertain assay across strata.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: average the stratumwise binary formula. Rebuttal: a marginal odds constraint is nonlinear in the averaged cells and cannot be imposed by independently selecting stratumwise odds ratios.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed is not a routine covariate extension because the association and assay constraints are both global.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the randomization-test rejection indicator by the event that the lower sharp benefit bound is positive, and derive the smallest arm-specific misclassification departure that changes that conclusion.
seed_details.destination_search: The anchor's warning accuracy concerns hypothesis-test conclusions and does not evaluate a cross-world benefit identified set.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: this is a direct renaming of warning accuracy. Rebuttal: the response would require optimizing a nonlinear partially identified endpoint, but without a new finite certificate it remains too close to the anchor and is dropped.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The close relabelling objection is not fully defeated, so this seed is not carried forward.

literature_map.settled: ZhangNieSoonLiu2013, Section 3.3, settles recovery of a positive binary joint table from two fixed margins and a fixed odds ratio. CiocaneaTeodorescuGabrielSjolander2025, Theorem 1, records the one-to-one marginal dependence parameterization and emphasizes compatibility. Molinari2008, equations (2.1)--(2.3), settles direct channel-matrix partial identification and generic sharpness.
literature_map.unoccupied_pair: No checked source optimizes the probability-compatible odds root over a single uncertain channel shared by randomized arms or proves a constant-size stationary-contact classification.
literature_map.subsumption_check: GabrielSachsJensen2024 covers ordinal clean endpoints and imperfect treatment assignment, not outcome-assay inversion. Molinari2008 permits nonlinear programming but does not state the candidate map. No closer checked paper subsumes the kernel.
literature_map.key_inspiration: Adapt ZhangNieSoonLiu2013's algebraic table reconstruction after Molinari2008's channel inversion, then classify the first-order boundary equations rather than invoking a black-box optimizer.

literature_map.settled: FanPark2010 derives limit theory for sharp treatment-effect-distribution bounds. GabrielSachsJensen2024 evaluates bootstrap coverage, documents regular-bootstrap undercoverage near parameter-space boundaries, and reports conservative \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) correction. KaidoMolinariStoye2019, Theorem 3.1, establishes uniform asymptotic calibrated projection for smooth targets under moment restrictions. ClopperPearson1934 gives exact primitive binomial intervals.
literature_map.unoccupied_pair: No checked source projects simultaneous exact trial-risk and gold-standard-validation binomial confidence sets through a shared-assay benefit map with a finite edge-complete evaluator and an explicit \(1/\kappa\) width modulus.
literature_map.subsumption_check: Generic Bonferroni containment is not novel and is credited. The finite four-region endpoint computation and contact-uniform width control depend on the new population envelope and are not subsumed by calibrated projection.
literature_map.key_inspiration: Adapt exact primitive inversion to obtain set containment first, then profile arm risks using root monotonicity so optimizer ties never enter the coverage proof.

literature_map.settled: RossColeEdwardsEtAl2024 identifies risks and risk differences by transporting misclassification parameters under conditional exchangeability and positivity. EdwardsZivichShookSaCole2026 explains Rogan--Gladen correction, incompatibility, and transportability. Molinari2008 allows restrictions rather than point knowledge of a channel.
literature_map.unoccupied_pair: No checked source defines or derives the smallest validation-to-trial channel discrepancy at which a probability-of-benefit sign conclusion changes under a latent association band.
literature_map.subsumption_check: The channel-restriction framework could contain the model abstractly, but it does not provide the critical-radius functional or its endpoint geometry. The seed survives novelty review but is not selected because it adds an unverified four-dimensional frontier before the shared-channel base case is settled.
literature_map.key_inspiration: Replace RossColeEdwardsEtAl2024's point transport substitution by a radius-indexed feasible channel set and define the first sign-changing radius as the M3 focal object.
